//: Story Phase 3, chapter 9: The Grand Stenchmaster Takes Command. The same evening as the trial. Garrick's office is by the mainmast: soapbox barrel (11,16), Stench Log on its crate (12,16), Garrick in front at (11,17). Crowd layout for the declaration is set up inside p3c1.declaration.

p3c1.begin.narrate: The sun is going down on the worst day in the history of the Queen Anne's Revenge.
The sea wind has carried off the worst of the cloud. Below decks, a stale yellow haze has settled in for the night, like a lodger with no intention of paying.
The crew have found ways to cope. None of them are good ways.

p3c1.deck: Rook has tied a wet sock over his nose. It is his own sock. It was not clean before it was wet.
Gristle the rigger is holding his breath. Every so often he has to stop, and every time he regrets it.
Even the ship's rat has improvised something.
hale: The haze below has thinned. The deck's breathable, as long as you stand upwind of the hatch and don't think about it.
hale[concerned]: ...That's why I came to find you.
hale: He's by the mainmast. Standing on a barrel. Wearing the galley curtain.
hale: He's asked for an audience. Actually he's asked for 'a brief all-hands', but nobody would come.
captain: Is he still on probation?
hale: Very much so. He keeps mentioning the frigate.

p3c1.deck.tutorial: Garrick is holding court by the mainmast. Speak with him.
p3c1.deck.title: A Necessary Promotion?

p3c1.garrick_reforms: garrick[proud]: Captain! Thank you for coming. Please, stand anywhere. The whole ship is my office now.
captain: Why are you wearing a curtain?
garrick[businesslike]: It's a mantle, Captain. And a pot. And this is a staff of office.
captain: That's the galley mop.
garrick: It WAS the galley mop. It has been promoted. Much like myself, shortly.
captain[annoyed]: Garrick. You were on trial four hours ago.
garrick[delighted]: And acquitted! Of the worst charges! On probation for the rest!
garrick[proud]: And then, if I may remind the court, I single-handedly repelled a naval frigate.
captain: You broke wind at it.
garrick[businesslike]: A strategic deterrent, Captain. The Navy turned around and went home. Nobody's ever made them do that before.
garrick: Which got me thinking about the ship's... situation.
garrick: I've been conducting what I'd call a short operational review.
garrick: Finding one. The treasure room has undergone an atmospheric rebranding.
garrick: Finding two. The treasure itself has experienced accelerated depreciation.
garrick: Finding three. The rest of the ship has been... what's the word... acquired.
captain[angry]: That's three ways of saying you ruined everything.
garrick[pretend]: It's three ways of saying the situation needs managing, Captain. By someone qualified.
garrick: I've started keeping records. It's all in the log. On the crate there.
garrick[smug]: Read it. Then we'll talk about the appointment.
captain: What appointment?
garrick[businesslike]: Read the log, Captain.

p3c1.garrick_reforms.tutorial: Inspect the Stench Log on the crate beside Garrick. Once you've read it, it stays in your pause menu.
p3c1.garrick_reforms.title: The Stench Log

p3c1.declaration: garrick[proud]: Well, Captain? Gripping, isn't it?
captain: 'Source: me.' Every page says 'Source: me.'
garrick[businesslike]: Accuracy is the first duty of an executive.
garrick: Speaking of which. If you'd step back a little, Captain? I'd like to address the crew.
garrick[proud]: Friends. Crewmates. Captain. Parrot.
squawks[insulting]: CAPTAIN Parrot.
garrick: Captain Parrot. Today, something happened aboard this ship.
mags[angry]: Something HAPPENED?
garrick[businesslike]: And whatever happened, it cannot be undone. I've looked into it. There's no undoing it.
garrick: So let's be honest about what it was.
garrick: It was not an accident. It was a merger. A hostile merger.
garrick[proud]: Beans. Cabbage. Onions. Garlic. Cheese. Sausage. And, very briefly, eel.
jim[angry]: I SAID no eel!
garrick[pretend]: And no eel was consumed, Jim, as per the terms of my probation. It was merely... present in the building.
garrick: Seven great ingredients. Each of them a leader in its field. Brought together under one roof.
garrick[proud]: My roof.
rook[disgusted]: He means his stomach.
garrick: The result was something no ship has ever survived before. And this ship survived it.
garrick: Which tells me two things. One, she's a fine ship.
garrick[businesslike]: And two, she's going to need someone to manage the aftermath. Someone with experience.
garrick: Someone with, if I may say so, first-hand knowledge of the product.
garrick[proud]: So, effective immediately, I hereby accept the position of...
Silence. Somewhere below decks, a hammock creaks.
captain: No.
garrick[businesslike]: I'm afraid it's already finalized, Captain.
captain: By whom?
garrick[smug]: By the only qualified applicant.
quill[concerned]: Captain, I feel I should point out that there is no such position.
garrick[delighted]: There is NOW, Quill! That's what makes it so exciting!
garrick[businesslike]: Now. The Grand Stenchmaster's duties, which I've taken the liberty of drafting.
garrick: Duty one. Odour inspection.
garrick: Every smell aboard this ship will be inspected, graded and filed. Ship smell. Wet rope smell. Fish smell. Pirate smell. Rotten food smell.
garrick[proud]: And, of course, the premium product.
brask[annoyed]: There's only one smell on this ship now, Garrick.
wick: It's true. I tried to smell the sea earlier. It smelled like you.
garrick[delighted]: Exactly! One smell! Think of the efficiency!
garrick: Duty two. The Stench Log. Location, severity, probable source, notes. Every whiff, on the record.
quill[disgusted]: He's using MY ledger, Captain. He used my good ledger.
garrick: Duty three. Evacuation zones.
garrick: Any part of the ship that the Grand Stenchmaster declares a zone will be evacuated, in an orderly fashion, until the Grand Stenchmaster says otherwise.
hale[resigned]: That's just the rule we already have about the hold.
garrick[businesslike]: It's that rule with a job title attached, Mister Hale. That's what management is.
garrick: And duty four. Classification.
garrick: Mild. Moist. Concerning. Severe. Catastrophic.
garrick[proud]: And Premium.
bob[concerned]: What's premium?
garrick[smug]: You'll know it when you smell it, Bob.
bob[queasy]: I think I already have.
gristle[queasy]: *GASP* ...Oh. Oh, that's worse. That's much worse. Why does holding it make it WORSE?
garrick[businesslike]: The air's been waiting for you, Gristle. It's built up. Classic Concerning.
squawks[furious]: Squawk! Stenchmaster! Fine! Duty FIVE!
squawks[outraged]: Feathers! BACK! Give them BACK!
garrick[pretend]: Ah. I'm afraid feathers are outside warranty, Captain Squawks.
squawks[furious]: WARRANTY?!
garrick: Terms and conditions. The fine print is very fine.
Every face on deck turns to you. Several of them are wearing socks.

then: captain[angry]: You are not the master of anything, Garrick. You're a stowaway on probation.
garrick[proud]: A stowaway on probation with a title, Captain. It changes the whole feel of the thing.
captain: Out of interest. What does the job pay?
garrick[businesslike]: Nothing at all, Captain. The position is its own reward.
garrick[greedy]: Although I've drafted a small executive salary, should you wish to show appreciation.
garrick: As I said. Its own reward.
captain[angry]: Get off the barrel, Garrick.
garrick[offended]: Captain, this barrel is the seat of the Stenchmastery.
garrick[pretend]: ...Which is why it's so well placed.

p3c1.declaration: garrick[proud]: In any case, the appointment is made. I'll be at my desk.
garrick: By which I mean this barrel. Or near it. Wherever the smell is strongest, really.
brask[disgusted]: Is he allowed to do that? Just... decide?
hale[resigned]: Nobody's ever tried it before. There's no rule against it.
quill[annoyed]: I'll write one.
garrick[smug]: File it with the Grand Stenchmaster's office, Quill. Page two.
p3c1.after: The crowd drifts apart, muttering. Nobody quite knows what just happened, only that it's been written down.
